title: Praying for other churches
hook: pray for the church down the road
tomorrow: seventy days of living it. what fits on one page?

segments.voice: That was a week of love and the church: the last layer, a peace given on a hard night, come and see, faithful honestly, hands needed. Yesterday's line: support it.
screen: `A WEEK OF LOVE AND THE CHURCH.` → `SUPPORT IT.`

segments.voice: The church down the road: a different sign out front, different songs, maybe a different way of baptizing or of sharing the bread. People drive past it every Sunday. What do you pray for a church that isn't yours? In Mark's Gospel, the disciples run into something like it, and they don't like it one bit.
screen: `THE CHURCH DOWN THE ROAD.` → `A DIFFERENT SIGN.` → `WHAT DO YOU PRAY FOR IT?`

segments.voice: John reports to Jesus: “Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.” Not one of us, so we stopped him. Jesus answers, “Forbid him not,” and then: “For he that is not against us is on our part.” On our part. The circle is wider than the disciples drew it. On his last night, in John's Gospel, Jesus prays for those who will believe later: “That they all may be one.” Churches today are divided in real ways, and they read that unity differently. Catholics, Orthodox Christians and Protestants each understand one church in their own way, and the differences are serious. Praying for another church doesn't erase them. It does something simpler. Paul tells the church at Philippi: “I thank my God upon every remembrance of you.” Praying for the church down the road, by name, turns a rival into a remembrance. And the whole week fits inside that prayer: love over everything, peace given, come and see, faithful honestly, hands, and support.
screen: `HE FOLLOWETH NOT US.` · `NOT AGAINST US, ON OUR PART.` · `THAT THEY ALL MAY BE ONE.` · `EVERY REMEMBRANCE, WITH THANKS.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE CHURCH.`

segments.voice: Say the name of one church near you that isn't your own, out loud. If you pray, thank God for the people inside it and ask good things for them; if not, hold them in mind with good will.
Praying for other churches. Holding the church down the road before God, by name, with thanks, as part of one body.
Your line: the whole church. He that is not against us is on our part. Two weeks of the heart and the church, done.

howItsDone: Christians pray for other churches in their own prayers and in services; some churches set aside special times of prayer for Christian unity, and neighboring congregations sometimes pray together.

chat.meaning: Jesus told the disciples, forbid him not: he that is not against us is on our part. Praying by name doesn't erase real differences; it gives thanks.

Philippi.meaning: a city whose church Paul thanked God for

Orthodox.meaning: a family of churches rooted in the Christian East

Protestants.meaning: Christians whose churches trace back to the Reformation
